title: How to organise the under-sink cabinet | Primary Bathroom
description:
To store cleaning supplies and backstock around the plumbing without ever hiding a leak.

This is the Under-Sink Cabinet in the Primary Bathroom. About 60-90 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Two pull-out bins clear of the P-trap, a pale tray on the cabinet floor with nothing stacked on it, one open bottle per job, and both shut-off valves in plain sight when the doors swing open.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Take it all out and line it up on the floor by job: glass, tub and tile, toilet, drain, polish.
Straighten: Build the bins around the P-trap instead of fighting it, keeping the joint and the valves visible.
Shine: Wipe the cabinet floor and look hard for a dark ring or a soft patch in the board, which is what a slow leak l
Safety: Never store bleach where it can tip into an ammonia-based cleaner, and never decant anything into a drink bott
Standardize: One open container per job, backstock capped at two.
Sustain: When you refill the hand soap at the basin, crouch and run your eyes over the cabinet floor and the trap joint

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
The P-trap and both shut-off valves stay in plain sight, one open bottle per job, backstock capped at two.
